title: Routes and params in Express
summary: Register a parameterized route and return JSON for both found and missing products.

scenario.briefing: The campus catalog exposes a small product API. The new detail route must return one product by id, and a missing id must produce a clear 404 instead of an empty success.

objectives.description: Apply the taught syntax in a working file.

hints: Use products.find and compare item.id with request.params.id.
When find returns undefined, answer with status 404 and a JSON error.

misconceptions.description: Returning a product instead of sending it.
misconceptions.feedback: Express does not serialize a returned value. Call response.json and let the handler finish.
misconceptions.testDescription: A found product is serialized as JSON.

misconceptions.description: Registering a broad route before a specific one.
misconceptions.feedback: The first matching route wins. Put the specific path first or make the broad handler account for the detail path.
misconceptions.diagnostic: Registering /products before /products/:id makes the broad handler answer first.

misconceptions.description: Believing a returned value is sent to the client.
misconceptions.feedback: Express ignores the return value of a route handler. The handler must call response.json or response.send.

sections.title: Routes match in order
sections.body: Express checks registered routes in sequence. A broad route such as /products can shadow a narrower one if it is registered first, so the specific path should be declared deliberately.

sections.title: Params are request data
sections.body: A colon marks a route parameter. After a match, the value is available on request.params under the same name.

sections.title: JSON is a response contract
sections.body: response.json serializes the value and sets the content type. Pair a missing resource with 404 so the client can distinguish absence from an empty result.

steps.title: Return one product by id
steps.prompt: Edit app.ts. Create the Express app, register GET /products/:id, return the matching product as JSON, and answer 404 when it is missing.

tests.description: The app is created and the parameterized route is registered.
The handler reads the id from route params and searches the catalog.
A missing product answers 404 with a JSON error.
A found product is serialized as JSON.

hints: Register app.get("/products/:id", ...) after the app is created.
Read request.params.id and find the product by id.
When find returns undefined, send status 404 and a JSON error.
Otherwise send the product with response.json(product).

statements.label: Route parameters are read from request.params after the route matches.
response.json serializes the value and sets a JSON content type.
Express matches routes in registration order, so a broader route can shadow a narrower one.
Returning a value from a route handler sends that value to the client.

steps.explanation: Express matches routes in the order they were registered and exposes path segments through request.params. The handler must write the response; a returned value is ignored.
hints: Check each statement against Express's request and response model.
Reject the claim that a returned value is sent automatically.
Confirm that route order determines which handler matches.
Select statements about params, JSON, and registration order.
